topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture on cancer causation and states what students should learn.

topics.label: Mutation-driven cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations accumulate and enable clonal evolution within a susceptible cell and permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposure contributes to cancer risk rather than cancer being attributable solely to chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma illustrating the cooperation between pathogens and cellular changes.

topics.label: How environmental exposures damage DNA
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular processes through which environmental exposures produce DNA damage and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how promotion enables previously initiated cells to grow into tumours without requiring the promoter itself to be directly mutagenic.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental context of carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain and recap why carcinogenic effects depend on the biological context in which exposure occurs.

topics.label: Tracing carcinogen exposure in human cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence from human cancers and populations can connect carcinogen exposure with cancer development.

topics.label: Experimental assessment of carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how experimental tests assess carcinogenic potential and why their results may not fully predict human cancer risk.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and the difficulty of making risk–benefit decisions.
